toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise in missed appointments is real and it comes from the Tidewell change. It is not the other things people suspected. Eastgate is on the old system and stayed at about 8%, so the bus cut and seasonal swings don't explain it. A clinical audit found miscoding accounts for only about 0.5 points of the 13.4%. Phone records show the day-before confirmation calls carried on at about 91–93% coverage, so the front desk didn't stop them. Written warnings would punish the wrong people. Hiding the DNA figure from the board would also be wrong.

Two things changed on the same day. The 48-hour text became a 7-day text, and booking lead times grew from about 19 to about 52 days. Both fit the data, and the patient comments point at both. Every specialty and appointment type rose, and we have no outcome data by lead time. So I can't say which one matters more, or whether it's both. I'm fairly sure of the exclusions and unsure about the split.

Next step: run the 8-week randomised test. Put the 48-hour reminder on half the templates, and ask the vendor for the appointment-level extract. Don't change the whole clinic's configuration yet. Keep reporting the DNA rate to the board, with a note that March and April are withheld.
